clue.text: Perhaps China contracted large plant

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, so TEA SET loses its last letter

parts.note: a china tea set is one kind of TEA SET; contracted, it loses its final T
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A botanist remarks that China has a big plant, or that some plant has shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C makes China look like the country; it is china crockery, a tea set.
explanation.definitionFit: The teasel is a tall prickly plant whose dried heads were once used to raise the nap on cloth.

clue.text: Muse drummer at opera houses

indicators.note: the phrase houses the answer, holding it inside its letters

parts.note: the letters run from the end of 'drummer', across 'at', into the start of 'opera'

explanation.surface: Muse's drummer is playing a set at an opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: Muse reads as the rock band, which makes 'drummer' look like part of the picture; Muse is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Stumped, ring representative and show annoyance

parts.note: st. is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
a Member of Parliament is an elected representative

explanation.surface: A baffled boxing promoter or politician storms off in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumped means baffled on the surface, but in cricket it is a way the batsman is out, recorded as st.
explanation.definitionFit: To stomp is to tread heavily, as someone does when they are cross.

clue.text: Country's old hotels refurbished

indicators.note: refurbished hotels are done up and rearranged, as the letters are

parts.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A nation's tired old hotels have been done up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is': the country is the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a small kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Seizing power, icon goes berserk with gun

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: something going berserk runs wild, so the letters fall into disorder

parts.note: used as written, joined to ICON by 'with'

explanation.surface: A coup: a famous figure grabs power and runs amok with a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seizing power' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'Seizing' and power is just the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouncing is springing on and grabbing something, so it means seizing.

clue.text: Arranged mountain climbing to accommodate the author's exercise regime

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means reading upwards
the reversed letters take I in as a guest

parts.note: the author refers to himself as I; the 's attaches the regime to him

explanation.surface: A writer describes an organised mountain climb built into his fitness routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The author' is the setter speaking of himself, so it gives I; 'Arranged' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of exercises for core strength and posture.

clue.text: Loose sex in France?

parts.note: un is the French for 'a'; in France the noun takes it in front

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about French attitudes to casual sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like an adjective describing sex; it is a verb, and 'a screw' said in French is 'un screw'. The question mark flags the Franglais.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose something is to loosen or release it, which is what you do when you unscrew it.

clue.text: Dance around that endlessly, again and again

indicators.note: again and again means the piece for that is written once and then twice more

parts.note: c. (circa) means around, as in dates

indicators.note: with no ends, 'that' keeps only its middle letters

explanation.surface: Instructions to dance round and round something, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Around gives C, from circa as used before approximate dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the cha-cha-cha, named for its triple step, is one Latin ballroom dance among many.

clue.text: Shot in leg, honourable chap's careless

indicators.note: shot means ruined or wrecked, so the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a gent, short for gentleman, is an honourable chap

explanation.surface: A gentleman who shot himself in the leg was careless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot in leg' reads as an injury; 'shot' is the instruction to rearrange IN LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent means failing to take proper care, that is, careless.

clue.text: Fairground Attraction sing in American English? Au contraire!

indicators.note: 'sing in American English' would put the song inside
'the opposite' flips 'in', so American English goes inside sing instead

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully

explanation.surface: A British band called Fairground Attraction singing with American accents, or not.
explanation.walkthrough: Fairground Attraction was a British pop band ('Perfect'), which makes 'sing' look natural; here the name is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A carousel, or merry-go-round, is a classic fairground ride.

clue.text: Silence irritable reggae musician

parts.note: aggy is British slang for aggressive or irritable

explanation.surface: Someone tells a bad-tempered reggae artist to shut up.
explanation.walkthrough: AGGY, from aggravation, is informal British for touchy or aggressive.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaggy is the Jamaican-American reggae singer behind 'Boombastic' and 'It Wasn't Me'.

clue.text: Rival school senior journalist has primarily touted for daughter

indicators.note: 'for' in the sense of 'in exchange for'

parts.note: a comp is a comprehensive, a British state secondary school

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of touted is kept

parts.note: first letter of touted; it replaces the D
D for daughter, the letter taken out

explanation.surface: A rival school's editor has been talking up his own daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touted for daughter' reads as promoting her; it means the T of touted takes the place of D in EDITOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: rivals and competitors are both people up against you for the same prize.

clue.text: Shock and anger reduced after a bit of laughter

indicators.note: a reduced IRE is shorter, losing its last letter
'after' in its sense of 'following in order' puts the anger piece behind the laughter piece

parts.note: laughter is written 'ha-ha-ha', and one bit of it is a single 'ha'
IRE is anger; reduced, it drops its E

explanation.surface: Laughter gives way to surprise and a fading temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Shock reads as surprise, but it is the noun for a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A shock of hair is a thick, untidy mop of it.

clue.text: Dodges international statisticians, except when in recession at the outset

indicators.note: something in recession is going backwards

parts.note: 'all save one' means all except one
the ONS is the UK's Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: Economists avoid questions, except when the economy is in recession.
explanation.walkthrough: Recession looks economic, fitting the statisticians; here it only signals backward movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Evasions are dodges: ways of avoiding a question or duty.

clue.text: What might change very revolutionary small island paramilitary force?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the next three pieces are written backwards

parts.note: S for small, as in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: Who could alter things: a radical paramilitary group on a tiny island?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small island' wants to be one piece like ISLE; it is S for small plus ELBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic-flavoured description: in maths and science a variable is precisely the quantity allowed to change, and the question mark flags the loose phrasing.

clue.text: Upset, a vocally discontented tosser is there until morning

indicators.note: upset letters are knocked over and jumbled
emptied of its contents, 'vocally' keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An annoyed, complaining idiot hangs around all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocally discontented' reads as grumbling out loud; it means the word 'vocally' emptied. Tosser is British slang for a contemptible man.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays over spends the night, so is there until morning.

clue.text: Mischievous wife chose to get rid of priest

indicators.note: 'to get rid of' means to throw out, so the priest's letter is thrown out of the word for chose

parts.note: PICKED means chose; the P goes
P for priest, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A naughty wife decided to get rid of the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: P for priest is a common abbreviation, as in Rev. and Fr.; here it is struck out of PICKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicked can mean playfully naughty, as in a wicked grin.

clue.text: Oil and gas circumventing limits of renewable energy

indicators.note: to circumvent is literally to go round, so GAS goes round the edge letters of renewable

parts.note: used as written; it wraps round RE

indicators.note: a word's limits are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Fossil fuels getting round the rules on green power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil and gas' reads as one industry; the definition is 'Oil' alone, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to oil a hinge and to grease it both mean to lubricate it.

clue.text: Makes certain criticism when head's not there with son

indicators.note: the first letter, the head, is missing
'with' in the sense of 'together with' attaches the son's letter to the rest

parts.note: CENSURE is criticism; beheaded, it loses its C

explanation.surface: A father makes sure he criticises his son only when the headteacher is away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a headteacher; it is the first letter of CENSURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, same form: he ensures it happens and he makes certain it happens say the same thing.

clue.text: American buggers bleat about dry bread

parts.note: the CIA plants bugs to listen in
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, or dry

explanation.surface: Americans moan about stale bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buggers' looks like an insult; it means people who plant listening bugs. 'Dry' wants to describe the bread, but it gives TT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciabatta is a flat Italian white bread.

clue.text: City firm suppresses drunken outburst before shareholder meeting cut short

indicators.note: something cut short loses its end, so the meeting's abbreviation drops its last letter
'before' in the sense of 'ahead of' puts the hiccup in front of the meeting

parts.note: AGM, annual general meeting, less its last letter

explanation.surface: A City firm hushes up a drunken scene before a shortened AGM.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City firm' reads as a London financial firm; City is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Chicago, the Windy City on Lake Michigan, is one example of a city.

clue.text: Alleged communist supports party dropping Republican

parts.note: RAVE is a party; its R moves to the end
R for Republican, the letter that drops

explanation.surface: A supposed communist backs a party that is ditching a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' looks like losing the R; instead the R falls to the bottom of RAVE, making AVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert, so averred means alleged or declared.

clue.text: Animals cold when taking temperature

parts.note: C for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: 'taking' in the sense of 'taking in' has the word for when absorb the temperature letter

explanation.surface: A vet takes the temperature of chilly animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' gives AS, as in 'as I left' meaning 'when I left'.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: cats are one kind of animal, so the broad word stands for the narrower one.

clue.text: Crustacean is bred with carp by mistake

indicators.note: a mistaken mix puts the letters in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A shellfish was accidentally crossbred with a carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link word joining definition to wordplay; its letters belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the spider crab, named for its long spindly legs, belongs to the crustaceans.

clue.text: Children initially enjoy SpongeBob SquarePants game with mates

parts.note: ch. is a dictionary abbreviation for children

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word that follows

explanation.surface: Kids love a cartoon and playing games with their friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Children initially' looks like one letter C; the abbreviation CH is used and 'initially' governs the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is the game ended by checkmate, and 'mates' reads as friends.

clue.text: Orphan returned home in natty trousers

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so it reads backwards
as a verb, trousers means pockets: the phrase holds the answer inside

explanation.surface: An orphan comes home wearing smart trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trousers' looks like clothing; it is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie is the heroine of the comic strip and the musical Annie.

clue.text: Surplus sandwiches left one boy wanting more

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Leftover sandwiches leave one hungry boy wanting more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food, fitting the hungry boy; it is the instruction to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist asks 'Please, sir, I want some more' in Dickens's novel.

clue.text: Matching silver jewellery item worn by celeb regularly

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: every other letter of celeb

explanation.surface: A celebrity always wears a matching silver ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn by celeb' reads as the celebrity wearing the ring; in the wordplay the ring wraps round the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that agree correspond, so agreeing means matching.

clue.text: Spot others failing to finish very strong coffee

indicators.note: both words are left unfinished, losing their last letters

parts.note: ESPY means spot; unfinished, it drops the Y
REST means others; unfinished, it drops the T

explanation.surface: Spotting others who can't finish their powerful coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very strong coffee' looks like the whole definition; 'very' gives SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is a strong black coffee forced through ground beans under pressure.

clue.text: One who pulls the boss at Christmas remains flushed over drinks

definitions.text: One who pulls the boss at Christmas

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: An office party: someone trying to seduce the boss, still red-faced from drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulls the boss' suggests office-party flirting (to pull is British slang for to pick up); the boss is Santa.
explanation.definitionFit: Dasher is one of Santa's reindeer, who pull his sleigh on Christmas Eve.
